title: Base-change conjugation of exceptional Weil data and counits
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Use the small pro-etale categories $D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ of [def-pur-conventions], for $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$: integral coefficients are completed and derived complete with uniform cohomological and Tor intervals, and field coefficients are scalar-localized/common-stage objects. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated finite type between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, with smooth geometric base change $f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$. Write $G_T=Lg_{T,\gamma}^*$, $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$, for [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]. Use a strict datum $\varphi_K:G_YK\simeq K$ on $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ as in [def-pur-tate-datum]. Write $P_fK=Lf^*K(d)[2d]$, $F_f=Rf_!$, $E_f=Rf^!$, $a_{f,K}=\gamma_{f,K}:P_fK\simeq E_fK$ for the purity map of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] and its specified coefficient transports [sk-thm-purity-transport], $\epsilon_{f,K}:F_fE_fK\to K$ for the counit of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and $t_{f,K}:F_fP_fK\to K$ for [def-pur-smooth-trace] and its coefficient transports. Use the source and exceptional data of [def-pur-tate-datum] and the compact-support datum $\varphi_{F_fM}=F_f(\varphi_M)e_{f,M}$ of [def-pur-compact-support-transport], where $e_f:G_YF_f\simeq F_fG_X$ is its specified semilinear exchange. All objects below are restricted to the constructible finite-Tor domains of these operations and comparisons.

Let $X'_0,Y'_0$ also be separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes and let $(f_0,f'_0,u_0,v_0)$ be a Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $u_0:X'_0\to X_0$, $v_0:Y'_0\to Y_0$, $f'_0:X'_0\to Y'_0$, all arrows separated finite type. Write $(f,f',u,v)$ for its geometric base change, $Q=Lu^*$, $Q_Y=Lv^*$, and give $Q_YK$ its transported strict datum under $Q_YG_Y\simeq G_{Y'}Q_Y$. Use the canonical comparisons $B_P:QP_f\simeq P_{f'}Q_Y$, $B_E:QE_f\simeq E_{f'}Q_Y$ and $B_F:Q_YF_f\simeq F_{f'}Q$. At finite coefficients $B_E$ is exactly the purity-composite smooth exchange [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange], for arbitrary $v$ in this finite-type setting. At the other stages use its specified purity transports [sk-thm-purity-transport], on their stated comparison domains, and the completed/localized/common-stage compact-support exchange; the assertion is on the common domain of these named comparisons. Put $a'=a_{f',Q_YK}$. The source identity (the base-change clause of [lem-pur-weil-tate-datum-transport], with the same $B_P$), the purity identity and the trace identity are
$$B_PQ(\varphi_{P_fK})=\varphi_{P_{f'}Q_YK}G_{X'}(B_P),\quad B_EQ(a_{f,K})=a'B_P,$$
$$Q_Y(t_{f,K})=t_{f',Q_YK}F_{f'}(B_P)B_F(P_fK),$$
with $QG_X\simeq G_{X'}Q$ inserted. With the actual mixed exchange of [lem-pur-weil-basechange-semilinear-pasting], the compact-support comparisons also obey
$$B_F(G_XM)Q_Y(e_{f,M})=e_{f',QM}G_{Y'}(B_F(M)),$$
under $Q_YG_Y\simeq G_{Y'}Q_Y$ and $QG_X\simeq G_{X'}Q$. The exceptional datum and counit reconstructed by
$$\varphi_{E_fK}=a_{f,K}\varphi_{P_fK}(G_Xa_{f,K})^{-1},\qquad\epsilon_{f,K}=t_{f,K}F_f(a_{f,K}^{-1})$$
satisfy the explicit conjugation and counit identities
$$B_EQ(\varphi_{E_fK})G_{X'}(B_E)^{-1}=a'B_PQ(\varphi_{P_fK})G_{X'}(B_P)^{-1}G_{X'}(a')^{-1}=\varphi_{E_{f'}Q_YK},$$
$$\begin{aligned}Q_Y(\epsilon_{f,K})&=Q_Y(t_{f,K})Q_YF_f(a_{f,K}^{-1})\\&=t_{f',Q_YK}F_{f'}(B_P)B_F(P_fK)Q_YF_f(a_{f,K}^{-1})\\&=t_{f',Q_YK}F_{f'}(B_PQ(a_{f,K}^{-1}))B_F(E_fK)\\&=\epsilon_{f',Q_YK}F_{f'}(B_E)B_F(E_fK).\end{aligned}$$
The compact-support data on these sources and targets agree under $B_F$ and the displayed mixed exchange, so the identities compare the actual labelled geometric purity, trace and counit diagrams. The integral mixed-exchange identity holds on the specified actual strict towers before derived limit, and field identities hold on localized/common stages. No scheme-Frobenius square is assumed Cartesian.

proof.text: All four geometric corners are separated finite type over $k$, and $f'$ is smooth of the same pure relative dimension $d$, by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] and [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. Thus the named comparisons apply on the stipulated common constructible finite-Tor domains. Put $a=a_{f,K}$ and $\psi=\varphi_{P_fK}$. The purity equivariance square in [thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace] says $\varphi_{E_fK}G_X(a)=a\psi$, and its specified trace is $t_{f,K}=\epsilon_{f,K}F_f(a)$ at all four stages. Right-compose the first equation with $G_X(a)^{-1}$ and the second with $F_f(a^{-1})$. This gives exactly the two recovery formulas in the statement, for $f$ and $f'$.

proof.text: Apply the base-change clause of [lem-pur-weil-tate-datum-transport] to obtain $B_PQ(\psi)=\psi'G_{X'}(B_P)$, where $\psi'=\varphi_{P_{f'}Q_YK}$. At finite coefficients [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange] defines $B_E=a'B_PQ(a)^{-1}$, hence $B_EQ(a)=a'B_P$ by cancellation. At the other stages these are the specified purity transports: [sk-thm-purity-transport] gives base-change compatibility for the same natural purity maps. The trace base-change clause of [thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity] gives $Q_Y(t_{f,K})=t_{f',Q_YK}F_{f'}(B_P)B_F(P_fK)$: specialize its smooth composition to $g=\mathrm{id}_Y$, so arbitrary base change of its $Z=Y$ is the present square. Its coefficient-transport clause, with [prop-pur-adic-reconstruction-trace-coherence] and [prop-pur-rational-purity-trace-coherence], gives the same identity for the specified completed and localized/common-stage traces. No additional domain of base change is asserted.

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-weil-basechange-semilinear-pasting] with $Q_X=Q$ and $B=B_F$. Its equation is precisely $B_F(G_XM)Q_Y(e_{f,M})=e_{f',QM}G_{Y'}(B_F(M))$. Its hypotheses hold since the square descends to $k_0$, all four arrows are separated finite type, and we retained its comparison domains. The cited statement supplies equality for the actual integral strict-tower transformations before derived limit, as well as for the field-stage images; it is not an inference from equality of evaluated maps.

proof.text:
Suppress only the named commuting-pullback identifications, and write $G'=G_{X'}$. The equality $B_EQ(a)=a'B_P$ implies $Q(a)^{-1}B_E^{-1}=B_P^{-1}(a')^{-1}$. Substitute this and the recovery formula into the conjugation expression to get
$$\begin{aligned}B_EQ(\varphi_{E_fK})G'(B_E)^{-1}
&=a'B_PQ(\psi)G'(Q(a)^{-1}B_E^{-1})\\
&=a'B_PQ(\psi)G'(B_P)^{-1}G'(a')^{-1}\\
&=a'\psi'G'(a')^{-1}=\varphi_{E_{f'}Q_YK}.
\end{aligned}$$
The second-to-last equality uses the source identity from Step 2; the last is Step 1 for $f'$. Only associativity, functoriality and cancellation of specified inverses were used.

proof.text:
Naturality of the specified natural compact-support comparison $B_F:Q_YF_f\simeq F_{f'}Q$, at $a^{-1}:E_fK\to P_fK$, reads
$$B_F(P_fK)Q_YF_f(a^{-1})=F_{f'}Q(a^{-1})B_F(E_fK).$$
Insert Step 2's trace identity in $Q_Y(\epsilon_{f,K})=Q_Y(t_{f,K})Q_YF_f(a^{-1})$, then apply this equation. The result is $t_{f',Q_YK}F_{f'}(B_PQ(a^{-1}))B_F(E_fK)$. From $B_EQ(a)=a'B_P$ one has $B_PQ(a^{-1})=(a')^{-1}B_E$. Substitution and Step 1 for $f'$ give $\epsilon_{f',Q_YK}F_{f'}(B_E)B_F(E_fK)$. These are exactly the four displayed lines of the counit identity.

source.place: Constituent-compatibility assembly paragraph; Returned Steps 1--3 and 8--10: shared reconstruction, mixed exchange, exceptional-datum conjugation and counit naturality calculation

proof.text:
To identify the compact-support labels, let $M=P_fK$ or $E_fK$, let $C:QM\simeq M'$ be $B_P$ or $B_E$, and put $\varphi_{QM}=Q(\varphi_M)$ under the stated pullback identification. Steps 2 and 4 give $C\varphi_{QM}=\varphi_{M'}G_{X'}(C)$. By [def-pur-compact-support-transport], the datum on $F_fM$ is $F_f(\varphi_M)e_{f,M}$. Naturality of $B_F$ at $\varphi_M$ and Step 3 yield
$$B_F(M)Q_Y(\varphi_{F_fM})=F_{f'}(\varphi_{QM})e_{f',QM}G_{Y'}(B_F(M)).$$
Naturality of $e_{f'}$ at $C$, followed by the equation for $C$, therefore gives
$$F_{f'}(C)B_F(M)Q_Y(\varphi_{F_fM})=\varphi_{F_{f'}M'}G_{Y'}(F_{f'}(C)B_F(M)).$$
This proves agreement of the actual source and target labels. All calculations are identities in the named categories; their tower and field interpretations use the actual comparisons already supplied in Steps 2 and 3. No scheme-Frobenius square is used.

Step 1: thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace gives φ_E·G_X(a)=a·ψ and Tr=ε∘Rf_!(γ) at all four Λ, so cancelling gives the recovery formulas. The trace identity comes from thm-pur-trace-normalization-transitivity with g=id_Y, e=0, Z=Y. Integral and field stages come from the two trace-coherence propositions, which transport thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence.

Step 3: the equation, hypotheses and domains of lem-pur-weil-basechange-semilinear-pasting match the item exactly, with B=B_F and e from def-exchange-projection.

Steps 4–6: I recomputed the conjugation chain, the four-line counit chain (naturality of B_F at a^{-1}) and the compact-support label identity (naturality of B_F and e_{f'}). All are correct and elementary.

Edge cases d=0, K=0, empty schemes, v=id and n=1 all check. Routes go through sk-thm-purity-transport, sk-thm-vanishing and sk-thm-smooth-purity, all reachable from sk-thm-sf-package; the Mathlib leaf is a tool. No step is a D1 relabelling.
